headline: This is the first housing pitch I've read that admits an alert isn't a safety check, and that honesty earns trust, but I can't tell whether it covers short-term sublets or what it will cost me.
must_fix: Say plainly that a short-term sublet (4-8 months) is a supported search, and that it watches the sources where sublets are actually posted. If it only works for 12-month leases, it's the wrong product for me.

State the money model up front: no fee before I've seen and confirmed a place, no 'priority alert' upsell, and no ID or documents required to set up a watch. Leaving this out of a brand position means the landing page will leave it out too.
would_flip_me: One line in the positioning saying that JIMS watches short-term sublets (including student boards) and never charges or asks for ID before you've confirmed a place.
in_character_reaction: Okay, this is the first one that doesn't put a shield on itself. 'An alert is a lead, not a guarantee' is the sentence I wish the last site had said to me. But I'm not looking for a lease, I need a room for six months, and nothing here tells me you'll even watch the Columbia board. And 'before the listing disappears' is the rush that got me scammed. Tell me it's free and that it covers sublets, and I'll try it.
